title: The Everything Crisis
gist: Teaser of Pratap Bhanu Mehta's review essay on books by Wooldridge and Acemoglu about liberalism's decline; the available text covers only the framing that liberals are most convinced of liberalism's end.

insights.claim: Liberals themselves are the people most convinced of liberalism's decline, and the past decade has produced an avalanche of Western essays and books mourning it.
insights.speaker: Pratap Bhanu Mehta
insights.so_what: The declinist narrative is itself a consensus view; contrarian opportunities may lie in stress-testing it.
insights.quote: Nobody is more convinced of the decline of liberalism than liberals themselves.

insights.claim: A rough consensus holds that the liberal ascendancy following the Cold War, with its expansion of democracy and free markets, is now over.
insights.speaker: Pratap Bhanu Mehta
insights.so_what: Frames the regime-change backdrop for assessing political and market risk premia.
insights.locator: A rough consensus has taken hold

insights.claim: The essay reviews Adrian Wooldridge's The Revolutionary Center and Daron Acemoglu's What Happened to Liberal Democracy? Remaking a Politics of Shared Prosperity.
insights.speaker: Pratap Bhanu Mehta
insights.so_what: Identifies the source books for the argument.
